question: As a registered nurse working under the team nursing model, what is your primary role on the ward?

options.A: Supervising the doctors during ward rounds
options.B: Performing every single procedure personally for all patients
options.C: Handling only the administrative paperwork for the ward
options.D: Acting as the team leader and taking overall accountability

explanation: Spot on! The registered nurse coordinates the group and takes ultimate responsibility for the care given, even when delegating specific tasks to others. You've got this!

question: Why was the team nursing model originally introduced in healthcare settings?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for registered nurses
options.B: To cope with nursing shortages and use various staff skills efficiently
options.C: To make patients pay less money for hospital admission
options.D: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Team nursing was designed to make the best use of available hands when professional nurses are limited in number. It's all about smart teamwork!

question: Which leadership style works best with the core philosophy of team nursing?

options.B: Strict autocratic control by auxiliary staff
options.C: Total absence of leadership or direction
options.D: Remote management from outside the hospital

explanation: Well done! Team nursing thrives when the leader respects every member and encourages collaboration instead of just barking harsh commands. Great ward dynamics!

question: How does the team nursing setup benefit junior staff and nursing students on the ward?

options.A: By exempting them from doing any physical patient care
options.B: By allowing them to write hospital policies
options.C: By giving them a supportive environment to learn from senior leaders
options.D: By forcing them to work alone without any supervision

explanation: That's right! Working closely with a registered nurse team leader gives students safe guidance and wonderful practical experience. Every shift is a learning win!

question: In a nursing team, who holds the legal responsibility for assessing patients and planning their care?

options.B: The team leader who is a registered nurse

explanation: Spot on! Assessing patients and planning care requires professional nursing judgment, which is the core duty of the registered nurse team leader.

question: You are working with a nursing assistant on your team. Which of these tasks is safe and appropriate to delegate to them?

options.A: Assisting a stable patient with morning bath and hygiene
options.B: Assessing a newly admitted patient with chest pain
options.C: Administering intravenous medications to a critical patient
options.D: Changing the comprehensive nursing care plan

explanation: Correct! Nursing assistants are wonderful helpers trained for basic comfort measures like hygiene, while medications and assessments need your professional skills.

question: What is the main goal of holding a team nursing conference at the start of a shift?

options.A: To conduct formal examinations for student nurses
options.B: To review patient assignments and plan the shift together
options.D: To discipline workers who came late to work

explanation: You got it! The brief conference helps the team connect, share updates, and organize duties so everyone knows what to expect before hitting the floor.

question: Why is clear, open communication during shift handovers so vital in team nursing?

options.A: It makes the shift last longer than necessary
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not speak to nurses
options.C: It prevents fragmented care and catches clinical changes early
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their health

explanation: Exactly! Sharing vital updates ensures everyone is on the same page regarding patient status, which keeps our patients safe from errors.

question: What is one of the biggest advantages of using the team nursing model?

options.A: Every single staff member performs the exact same tasks
options.B: Cost-effective use of mixed staff cadres working together
options.C: Complete elimination of any need for supervision
options.D: Patients never have to interact with nursing assistants

explanation: Spot on! Team nursing lets hospitals blend different skill levels efficiently, making patient care well-organized and resourceful.

question: What is a major risk or downside if team leadership on the ward is weak?

options.A: Patients refusing to take any hospital medications
options.B: Automatic promotion of all junior staff members
options.C: Blurred responsibilities and fragmented patient care
options.D: Doctors taking over all nursing responsibilities

explanation: That's right! When leadership lacks clear direction, team members get confused about who is supposed to do what, leading to gaps in patient care.

question: In which care delivery model are duties divided strictly by tasks—like one nurse only giving medications and another only doing wound dressings?
explanation: Correct! Functional nursing focuses on getting specific tasks done across all patients, rather than assigning a whole patient to one nurse.

question: How does team nursing differ from total patient care?

options.A: Total patient care involves no registered nurses at all
options.B: Total patient care is only used in surgical operating theatres
options.C: Team nursing uses a mix of different staff cadres to care for a group of patients
options.D: Team nursing requires one registered nurse to do everything alone

explanation: Well done! Total patient care means one nurse handles everything for a patient, while team nursing shares the workload among a group of mixed staff.

question: What is a major challenge when trying to run team nursing in many Nigerian hospital wards?

options.A: High patient-to-nurse ratios and severe staff shortages
options.B: Complete lack of patients admitted to the wards
options.C: Too many nursing assistants available for every shift
options.D: An excessive number of registered nurses on every ward

explanation: Spot on! Shortages of professional staff make leading teams tough because nurses get overworked and stretched across too many duties.

question: If your ward has a severe shortage of nursing assistants, what is a likely result for you as the registered nurse team leader?

options.A: Being exempted from all clinical ward duties
options.B: Having more time to focus purely on complex patient management
options.C: Spending extra time performing basic domestic or clerical chores

explanation: That's correct! When support staff are missing, professional nurses often have to step in to cover basic tasks, which cuts into time for leadership and assessments.
